theory: State the integer index domains: factorial coefficients require $0\le r\le n$, the consecutive-coefficient ratio requires $1\le r\le n$, Pascal's two-neighbour form requires $0\le r<n$, and the hockey-stick sum requires $0\le r\le n$. Without these restrictions, the theory presents expressions with undefined factorials or denominators as unrestricted identities; the identities themselves are correct and no worked examples are supplied.
